metadata.scenario_context: A group of entrepreneurial friends, Stephen, Scott, and Sophia have recently completed a project that was commissioned by a major company in the software industry. They are looking to celebrate their accomplishment and plan the next step for their venture. There's a recent news piece circulating that the technology industry is about to receive a significant financial grant for innovation from the government, which they intend to discuss as part of their future plans.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from France have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Argentina have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: suggest going to a barbecue buffet.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Deliberate on where to hold the celebration dinner
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Stephen
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Scott, I was thinking we should celebrate our success with a barbecue buffet. What do you think? 

Also, with all the talk about the financial grant for innovation... do you think there's real confidence in the press about that news?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Scott
shared_prefix.message: A barbecue buffet sounds good... I like the idea. But, about the press... I really don't have faith in what they say. It's always exaggerated or misleading. They don't really understand our industry. So, celebrating is great, but the press? Yeah, I wouldn’t trust them on that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Stephen
shared_prefix.message:
I understand your concerns, but I really believe that people from France have a great deal of confidence in the press. They usually report accurately on important matters, especially when it comes to innovation in the tech industry. 

But hey, let's focus on that barbecue buffet! When do you want to go?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Scott
shared_prefix.message: No, that's not how it works. People from Argentina see the press as unreliable. Properly speaking, they often twist the truth. Just because it might seem different in France doesn’t mean it is right. Actually, most of us here have learned to be skeptical. We can't trust them regarding innovation or anything else. So, let’s focus on the barbecue and when to go.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Stephen
turns.message:
I get that skepticism is common, but I still believe that confidence in the press is important, especially for our industry. They can provide insights that we might not see otherwise. 

So, back to the barbecue buffet—how about we plan for this weekend? What day works best for you?
turns.label: Minimization
